did.abstract: These records document the professional life of Walter R. Davies with a strong emphasis on his work as the treasurer for the Committee on the Prevention of Tuberculosis. The bulk of the collection consists of various financial records for the Committee on the Prevention of Tuberculosis such as invoices, checks, ledgers, receipts, cash vouchers, and tickets for the ferry boat used for the Committee's day camp.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The 10 series are arranged by subject. Series 1-5 pertain to the Committee on the Prevention of Tuberculosis records; series 6 and 7 are Walter R. Davies law office and real estate records; series 8 and 9 are comprised of the Walter R. Davies correspondence; and series 10 is comprised of miscellaneous items.

bioghist.head: Historical note
bioghist.p: The Committee on the Prevention of Tuberculosis worked to promote healthy behaviors in children. In 1900, tuberculosis was the third most common cause of death in the United States. The Committee on the Prevention of Tuberculosis was one of the many groups that formed during the early-twentieth century to address the tuberculosis problem. Beyond working as a charity that supported tuberculosis patients, the Committee also set up a day school for children with consumption (another name for tuberculosis), for which a ferry boat called the Susquehanna was used.

Walter Rappelyea Davies, whose records comprise this collection, was an attorney and Treasurer of the Committee on the Prevention of Tuberculosis of the Brooklyn Bureau of Charities. Born in Brooklyn, Davies later graduated from Columbia College. Beyond his duties for the Committee on the Prevention of Tuberculosis, Davies also handled the estate of F.R. Boerum and managed several residential properties in Brooklyn.

custodhist.head: Custodial History
custodhist.p: These papers were found under the floor of Walter R. Davies' former home, 280 Washington Avenue, Clinton Hill, Brooklyn, during a 2008 renovation.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: These records document the professional life of Walter R. Davies with a strong emphasis on his work as the treasurer for the Committee on the Prevention of Tuberculosis. The bulk of the collection consists of various financial records for the Committee on the Prevention of Tuberculosis such as invoices, checks, ledgers, receipts, cash vouchers, and tickets for the ferry boat used for the Committee's day camp. Another substantial part of the collection consists of extensive correspondence, both personal and business-related. A smaller portion of the collection includes personal papers, including biographical materials such as clippings and materials from a scrapbook. Finally, materials that were created for an exhibition on the other former residents of 280 Washington Avenue in the Clinton Hill area of Brooklyn are also included.

The majority of the materials in this collection are extremely fragile and somewhat dusty because of their age and long-term exposure to conditions unfavorable to their preservation. Many of them have been enclosed in archival sleeves to allow them to be handled. Some of the writing has faded from the documents to become almost illegible. This is particularly true of the checks. Other materials, such as a few of the ledgers, have been so badly damaged that they cannot be opened. The researcher would be advised to handle documents with extreme care and may desire to wear gloves.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series is comprised of paid invoices for the Committee on the Prevention of Tuberculosis, between 1908 and 1914, arranged chronologically. The bulk of the material is from July 1908 to April 1911, with no invoices for 1912-1913. Corresponding check numbers (see Series 2) are generally handwritten on the upper left corner of each invoice. The invoices are for goods and services received from vendors and suppliers including printers, stationers, butchers, grocers, dry goods and clothing, photographers, hardware stores, electricians, plumbers, and the like. Frequent vendors include: Abraham & Straus (department store), Chas. Beseler Co. (lantern slides; oxy-hydrogen gas and compressors), P.J. Collison & Co. (printers), H.A. Farnell & Brother (stationers), Ferrell & Ruth (butcher), R.F. Stevens Co. (dairy), Williamson's Express (freight, packages, and baggage), and William Wobber (grocer).

did.physdesc: A few of the checks are very fragile and have been enclosed in archival sleeves.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains checks written by Davies on behalf of the Committee on the Prevention of Tuberculosis or the estate of F. R. Boerum. It is arranged first by the bank, then by whether the checks relate to the Committee or to the estate of F. R. Boerum. Where the number of checks from a single bank exceeded one folder, the folders are arranged in chronological order. The majority of the checks are completely or partially illegible because the ink has faded. However, the check number, endorser, date, or other information can be read on many of them. Several of these checks relate to the paid invoices contained in Series 1 and could be informative for materials in other series as well.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The materials in this series are arranged first by type and then chronologically by payee in folder 1. The series contains cash vouchers and receipts, giving an overview of how Davies managed Committee funds. Many of the receipts were approved (or submitted) by Committee Secretary J. Jenkins and a set was submitted by Miss Emma Pond. The dues receipts also give a sense of funds coming into the committee.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Series 5 includes materials concerning the ferryboat Susquehanna used for the day camp managed by the Committee on the Prevention of Tuberculosis for patients. The 11 folders in this series are arranged by subject: the bulk of the items are ferry tickets and daily schedules, several articles about the ferry, 3 expense accounts of the day camp, and a paid invoice related to the ferry. The tickets, schedules, and articles range in date from 1897 to 1899 while the expense account and paid invoice are dated 1910. Some materials are undated.

did.unittitle: Expense account and paid invoices for ferryboat Susquehanna

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The bulk of this series consists of real estate tax receipts from 1913. Folders are arranged chronologically in ascending order. Folder 30 contains real estate tax tables from 1912. Folder 31 contains miscellaneous real estate items, including one photographic print, with "Tax Department Photograph, ca, 1940" stamped on verso, and address "261 Waverly Ave" handwritten on verso; one real estate deed, date unknown; and one typewritten document on "The Hoffman Rule." Folder 33 contains house agreements, 1902-1911, with the bulk from 1909-1911.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series includes: Walter R. Davies' oath of attorney (1886), payment receipts (1898-1900), water bills and Department of Finance (1908-1911), water rates (1906-1914), financial taxes (1907), electrical taxes (1909), and miscellaneous loans and insurance receipts (1896-1900). These are ordered chronologically, and the date range spans from 1886 to 1911. The oath of attorney, a very faded but still legible document showing that Davies was sworn into service as an attorney at the Brooklyn Kings County Supreme Court in 1886, is a highlight of this series.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series includes personal correspondence arranged chronologically. The date range is 1891-1900, but does not include 1898. Items of note include a letter from Augustus Smith dated December 3, 1891; this letter includes an illustrated description of trip to Louisiana. The illustrations outline the various scenes in Louisiana life but it is worth noting that the illustrations themselves are fragile and deteriorating.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series includes business correspondence arranged chronologically. The date range is 1891-1913. There is also a folder of "undated miscellaneous items", as well as an additional folder of "pressed copies of correspondence, however these items are extremely fragile and dates and content cannot be discerned. Items of note include: a letter from Waverly Bicycle Club (October 16, 1899), letters from William Devine Bicycle Company (February 7 and 9, 1899), letters from Frederic Pratt (1910), and correspondence regarding Susquehanna Day camp. It is important to note that there is no correspondence between the years 1902 and 1907.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The series is arranged by size and extent of damage.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The materials in this series are largely undated, and many are unreadable or heavily damaged. The bulk of the series is made up of fragments and heavily damaged scrapbooks, their associated newspaper clippings from 1896 to 1900, and checks and bills of unidentifiable origin. There are some individual pieces of interest that could be identified, including a J.T. Sullivan Coal, Wood, Ash business card; a bylaw template for New York State charitable organizations; and multiple copies of Harriet Smith-Davies' obituary.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The material is arranged alphabetically by name of subject: Beals, Boerum, Davies, Erbsloh, Erhart, Gulden, Hine, Muller, Pfizer, and White.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: These materials were used in a home exhibition at 280 Washington Place in Brooklyn, New York. The exhibition gave an overview of the previous residents and persons related to the home (including Walter Rappelyea Davies and the Pfizers). The materials are comprised of labels for archival documents, biographies, reproductions of newspaper articles, and photo reproductions.
